signature.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
signature.detail: Thousands of vermilion torii gates wind up the mountain, making this Japan's most photographed shrine. It is free and open 24 hours; go before 8am or after 5pm to avoid the crowds.

signature.name: Kinkaku-ji
signature.detail: The gold-leaf-covered pavilion reflected in a mirror pond is Kyoto's postcard image. Open 9am-5pm; arrive at opening time for the calmest visit.

signature.name: Kiyomizu-dera
signature.detail: A vast wooden stage juts over the hillside, offering sweeping views of the city. The temple is open from 6am, so early morning is the quietest; it's a 20-minute walk uphill from the bus stop.

signature.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
signature.detail: Walking through towering green bamboo is a quintessential Kyoto experience. It is free and always open; visit before 8am to enjoy the path without crowds.

signature.name: Gion District
signature.detail: Kyoto's historic geisha quarter is lined with wooden machiya houses and teahouses. Wander the side streets in the evening for the best atmosphere, and remember that private lanes are off-limits to photography.

signature.name: Nijo Castle
signature.detail: A UNESCO-listed castle famous for its 'nightingale' floors that squeak underfoot. Open 8:45am-5pm (closed some Tuesdays in winter); allow two hours to explore the palace and gardens.

signature.name: Ginkaku-ji
signature.detail: The Silver Pavilion, set in a tranquil moss garden, is a masterpiece of Zen aesthetics. Open 8:30am-5pm; combine with a walk on the nearby Philosopher's Path.

signature.name: Ryoan-ji
signature.detail: Japan's most famous dry landscape garden, with 15 rocks arranged on raked white gravel. Open 8am-5pm; sit on the veranda and try to see all 15 rocks at once.

signature.name: Sanjusangendo
signature.detail: A long hall housing 1,001 gilded statues of Kannon, the goddess of mercy. Open 8:30am-5pm; photography is not allowed inside, so take your time to absorb the sight.

signature.name: Tenryu-ji
signature.detail: A major Zen temple with a stunning pond garden backed by the Arashiyama hills. Open 8:30am-5pm; the garden is especially beautiful in autumn.

transport: Bus or subway $2-3 a ride; day pass $6-10
